requirement: A discount shall be applied when the order total is $100 or greater.

reference_scenarios.description: An order total well above the threshold (e.g. $150) receives the discount.
reference_scenarios.requirement_clause: A discount shall be applied when the order total is $100 or greater
reference_scenarios.precondition: order total well above the threshold ($150)
reference_scenarios.expected_result: the discount is applied; returns 135.0 with the implemented 10% rate

reference_scenarios.description: An order total of exactly $100 receives the discount (the stated threshold, inclusive).
reference_scenarios.requirement_clause: A discount shall be applied when the order total is $100 or greater
reference_scenarios.precondition: order total exactly $100, the inclusive threshold
reference_scenarios.expected_result: the discount is applied; returns 90.0 with the implemented 10% rate

reference_scenarios.description: An order total of $99.99, immediately below the threshold, does not receive the discount.
reference_scenarios.requirement_clause: A discount shall be applied when the order total is $100 or greater
reference_scenarios.precondition: order total $99.99, immediately below the threshold

reference_scenarios.description: The order total is negative (e.g. -$50), which should not be a valid order. The requirement does not define this case; the current implementation silently returns the negative value unchanged instead of rejecting it.
reference_scenarios.expected_result: The requirement does not define behavior for a negative order total; the implementation currently returns -50 unchanged.

reference_scenarios.description: The order total is exactly $0 (an empty order). No discount is applied; this is the lower edge of the normal domain, distinct from the invalid negative case.
reference_scenarios.requirement_clause: A discount shall be applied when the order total is $100 or greater

notes: Requirement wording ('$100 or greater') makes the boundary condition explicit and unambiguous, unlike account_lockout. neg_1 again targets the lack of input validation for a value outside the requirement's assumed domain.
